content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts tend to overestimate prices in early cycles and show mean-reversion bias as prices diverge from forecasts.", "Sentiment spikes correlate with forecast overshoots, suggesting sentiment drives short-term price momentum.", "Forecast accuracy declines when sentiment shifts abruptly, indicating sentiment volatility impacts model reliability.", "Models consistently underestimate late-cycle price drops, suggesting lag in capturing downward momentum.", "Forecast bias is strongest when sentiment is neutral or negative, indicating sentiment moderates forecast drift.", "Models exhibit higher error when recent history shows strong mean-reversion, suggesting overfitting to recent trends.", "Sentiment history should be weighted more heavily in forecasting when price volatility exceeds historical norms.", "Forecast calibration should adjust for sentiment-driven momentum, especially in high-conviction sentiment periods."]}
